intent: Put the screen-locker status back on the i3 bar, so a miscounting or disarmed locker is visible without being asked. The GTK tray icon it replaces had been commented out of ~/.config/i3/config since 2026-08-21, and in that window the locker counted one workout twice, believed the week met at 5/5 when the real total was 3, and skipped enforcement for two ISO weeks with nothing on the machine saying so.
scope: Non-goal: the block never mutates locker state; clicking only opens the read-only UI
Depends on screen-locker-web.service (127.0.0.1:8770) from the screen-locker repo
changes: New block renders '<count>/<minimum> · <gaming budget>' from GET /api/status, coloured by compliance_state (green ok / yellow warn / red lock).

Arming from GET /api/health overrides the compliance colour: a timer that is disabled or has no next trigger shows 'DISARMED' in red, because a locker that cannot fire is the worse failure and the one that hides.
A dead status server renders the last known value marked '(stale)' in orange, or 'status server down' in red when there is no cache — never a blank block.
Missing curl/jq degrades to a visible marker rather than an empty block or a bash error.

verification.evidence: Prints '💪 3/5 · 6h' / '💪 3/5' / '#F1FA8C' — 3/5 is the corrected weekly count, 6h the cut gaming budget for a day with no workout.
With cache: '💪 3/5 · 6h (stale)' in orange. After rm of the cache: '💪 status server down' in red. Restored to '💪 3/5 · 6h' once the unit was started again.

Block visible in the HDMI-0 bar between PC:warn and the 23:00 shutdown countdown, rendering '💪 3/5 · 6h' in yellow. i3blocks does not re-read its config on i3-msg reload alone; the running process had to exit first.

risks: Two curl calls every 30s. Both are loopback with --max-time 2, so a hung server delays the block by at most 4s rather than wedging the bar.
The block reports the gaming budget using its own 8h/6h constants. If steam-backlog-enforcer's configured values change, this display drifts from the enforcer until updated.
rollback: Remove the [screen_locker] stanza from linux_configuration/i3blocks/config, delete linux_configuration/i3blocks/screen_locker.sh and the ~/.config/i3blocks symlink, then i3-msg reload and kill the running i3blocks so it re-reads the config.
After rollback, confirm the bar still renders the remaining blocks (cpu, gpu, memory, disk, volume, ethernet, claude_usage, pc_startup, shutdown_countdown, time).
